industry.structure: Organised Indian lead-acid batteries are a two-player market: Exide (FY26 standalone revenue Rs17,269 cr) and Amara Raja (Rs13,549 cr) supply most car and two-wheeler OEMs and lead the replacement market; Amara Raja leads telecom (>60% share across lead and lithium, Q1FY27 call) and Exide leads most other industrial lines. Both now also sell lithium-ion packs and are building cell plants.
industry.demand: Demand comes from new vehicles (OEM), the replacement cycle (a car battery lasts ~3-4 years), home energy (inverters, tubular batteries), industrial back-up (UPS, data centres, railways, power, solar) and exports. Auto OEM volumes jumped after the September-2025 GST cut (Amara Raja's 4W OEM +24%, 2W +35% in Q1FY27); management sees the lead-acid market growing ~9-10% a year in volume over the medium term (Q1FY27 call).
industry.threat: Lithium-ion is replacing lead-acid in telecom towers (Amara Raja's lithium telecom volumes +50% in Q1FY27 while lead-acid telecom shrinks), e-rickshaws and 3W, and will take EV traction batteries; 12V starter batteries in petrol and diesel vehicles remain lead-acid.
industry.costs: Lead and alloys are ~70% of the material bill and plastics ~10% (Q4FY26 call); sulphuric acid, plastics and tin rose sharply in FY26-Q1FY27; prices were raised 5-6% in Q4FY26, ~3% in June-2026 and 2-3% in August-2026; B2B (OEM) price changes lag.
industry.lithium: India's lithium demand ~15 GWh in FY26 rising to ~100 GWh by FY31 (Nuvama, 11-Aug-2026); management sees a 100-130 GWh market and aims for 15-20% share of cells; Indian cells cost 15-20% more than Chinese (Q1FY27 call). Four lead-acid makers are also building lithium capacity; OEMs also build their own (Q1FY27 call). A re-opened 10 GWh PLI tranche was being bid (Q1FY27 call).

named: Amara Raja Enterprises Pvt Ltd (formerly RNGalla Family Pvt Ltd; promoter, Galla family)
ownership.src: Screener.in shareholding (Jun-2026 BSE pattern); Q1FY27 deck (shareholding at 30-Jun-2026); AR FY26 (promoter holding 6,01,45,316 shares); Nuvama 11-Aug-2026 (pledge 0%)

moat.brand: Amaron is the second-best-known battery brand in India, with 1,500+ direct partners and 1,00,000+ points of sale; a D2C service pilot (Amaron Assist) started in Q1FY27 (Q1FY27 deck).
moat.scale: ~70 mn automotive units a year; own lead recycling at Cheyyar (100,000 t refining capacity, ~88% of lead from recycled sources, but scrap prices currently make recycled lead cost the same as LME lead: Q1FY27 call).
moat.oem: Supplies most 2W and 4W OEMs; OEM volumes +24% (4W) and +35% (2W) in Q1FY27; >60% of telecom across lead and lithium.
moat.pricing: EBITDA margin 15-17% in FY15-21, 14-15% in FY23-24, 11.4% in FY26 and 10.1% in Q1FY27 (Screener standalone): input costs are passed on late; traded goods now ~16% of revenue at lower margins.

critiques: Margins have halved their premium: standalone EBITDA margin fell from 16-18% (FY15-16) to 11.4% (FY26) and 10.1% (Q1FY27); management's 13-14% aim has no date (Q4FY26 call).
Rising trading content: traded goods were Rs2,127.5 cr (16% of revenue) in FY26 and ~15% of lead-acid revenue in Q1FY27, diluting gross margin (AR FY26 note 22; Q1FY27 call).

Lithium returns: MOFSL is cautious (OEM tie-ups limit the market, low margins, technology risk); the Gotion technology tie-up did not happen (ICICI Direct, Jun-2026); cells cost 15-20% more than Chinese ones; the 16 GWh plan is now an 'ambition' (Q1FY27 call).

Funding beyond Rs2,500 cr: the parent has turned from net cash to a small net debt (borrowings Rs271 cr vs cash Rs115 cr at Mar-26, AR FY26); management keeps 'other options' open for later capacity (Q1FY27 call).
Family pay: the Chairman and two Executive Directors drew Rs39.4 cr in FY26, ~4% of standalone profit (AR FY26).
Bulls (Nuvama, Anand Rathi) see BESS as a near-term earner (Anand Rathi: BESS PAT Rs134 cr by FY30E); management guides only 5-8% operating margins on imported cells.

governance.board: 6 directors: 3 executive from the promoter family (Jayadev Galla as Chairman, MD & CEO; Harshavardhana and Vikramadithya Gourineni as Executive Directors) and 3 independent (Annush Ramasamy, Dr Amar Patnaik, Radhika Shapoorjee); the chair is not independent
governance.auditor: Joint auditors Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP and K.S. Rao & Co; FY26 reports unmodified (AR FY26).
governance.relatedParty: ARCSPL sells recycled lead to the company; loans of Rs120 cr to ARPSL; equity into ARACT; Mangal Industries (promoter group) supplied plastic components until its battery-components business was demerged into the company.
